_README: W12b's channel pool. AUTHORED, NEVER INFERRED.
`channel_id` is the authority and `handle` is a convenience: handles change,
channel ids do not. Every id here is resolved once by
`python -m core.video.resolve_channels` against the YouTube Data API and
pasted in. A NULL id is not a placeholder to be filled in by guessing --
core.video.channels REFUSES to load an entry whose id is null or whose id
still looks like a handle, so the refresh path cannot run against a guess.
`accent` is authored on the CHANNEL, never detected from a video, and has
exactly two values by operator ruling (2026-08-30): two accents that are
actually rotated beat six with no channels behind them. Adding a third later
is a data change -- one value here and one literal in migration 019's CHECK.
A NULL accent is refused for the same reason a null id is.
`track` uses the vocabulary of `users.track_weights` (migration 012) so that
`topic_match` compares like with like: life | curiosity | work.
PRODUCT-PRINCIPLES §3: this file is GLOBAL CONFIGURATION THAT BECOMES
PER-USER IF THE TWO LEARNERS' INTERESTS DIVERGE. Today both share the pool
and `users.track_weights` does the per-learner work. When it diverges it
gains a users-keyed table, not a second file.
_POOL_BALANCE: The target is Life & Social 50 / Curiosity 30 / Work 20 (PRD §4.6).
BY CHANNEL COUNT THIS POOL IS 55 / 36 / 9, AND IT DOES NOT MEET THE TARGET.
That is recorded here rather than left to be discovered from the assignments.
It does not have to meet it, and the reason is worth stating so nobody
'fixes' it later: THE WEIGHTS ARE SCORING TERMS, NOT QUOTAS. `topic_match` is
one 0.20 term in a weighted sum (PRD §7.2); nothing enforces a ratio, and the
realised mix runs roughly channel-proportional. A slice that promised
50/30/20 and delivered 55/36/9 would be reporting a target as a result.
THE WORK TRACK HAS ONE CHANNEL, AND THEREFORE ONE ACCENT. So `accent_rotation`
(0.15) and `topic_match` (0.20) are structurally in conflict there: a work
video can only ever be British. Filed as a known issue with a target rather

channels.name: English Teacher Claire
channels.why: Conversational everyday English at a deliberate pace; operator-approved as a Life & Social anchor.

channels.name: Friends (official)
channels.why: Real scripted conversation between friends -- the register PRD §4.6 exists to protect, and the one thing a teaching channel cannot supply.

channels.name: Easy English (street interviews)
channels.why: Unscripted strangers answering a question in the street: the closest thing in the pool to how people actually speak.

channels.name: Learn English With TV Series
channels.why: Connected speech and reductions taught from real clips, which is PRD §7.5's stated failure mode for a learner with good grammar.

channels.name: Speak English With Vanessa
channels.why: Everyday phrases in full sentences at natural speed; a steady mid-B1 supply.

channels.name: Rachel's English
channels.why: Explicit General American pronunciation and reductions; the American half of the accent rotation.

channels.name: TED-Ed
channels.why: Short narrated explainers on one idea; dense but clearly structured, and the transcripts are unusually clean.
channels._unresolved: accent NOT AUTHORED -- see _UNRESOLVED below. TED-Ed is the structural case, not merely the uncertain one.

channels.name: Vox
channels.why: Explanatory journalism; real adult subject matter rather than material written for learners.

channels.name: Johnny Harris
channels.why: One narrator, strong narrative drive; holds attention through a longer runtime than the pool's average.

channels.name: BBC Learning English (News Review)
channels.why: Current news retold with the vocabulary made explicit; the British half of the accent rotation.

channels.name: English with Lucy
channels.why: The pool's only Work-track channel; formal register and British pronunciation.

_UNRESOLVED: THREE ACCENTS ARE DELIBERATELY NULL, AND THIS IS A FINDING RATHER THAN AN
OMISSION. `accent` is authored, and authoring it means knowing it -- writing
a plausible value would be the same defect as writing a plausible channel id.
@EnglishTeacherClaire     -- not established by the author of this file.
@LearnEnglishWithTVSeries -- not established by the author of this file.
@TEDEd -- NOT UNCERTAINTY BUT A STRUCTURAL MISMATCH. TED-Ed lessons are
narrated by many different voices, so the channel HAS NO SINGLE ACCENT and
a per-channel field cannot hold the truth about it. The three honest
options are: drop TED-Ed from the pool; author the accent per VIDEO for
this channel only (a schema change, since `videos.accent` is currently
copied from the channel); or accept a nominal value and know that
`accent_rotation` is lying by that much. THIS IS THE OPERATOR'S RULING TO
MAKE, and it is filed rather than chosen here.
Until each is filled, core.video.channels refuses to load that entry and
`core.video.refresh` will not poll it. The pool runs with the eight that are
complete; it does not silently run with a guess.
